title: Quarapin (Round Swamp)
summary: A Huntington swamp placename remembered as the planting place of a Native person named Quarapin.
introduction_content: Quarapin is recorded as a round swamp in Huntington. The name is attached to Quarapin, a Native person who formerly planted there.
history_content: The surviving entry identifies Quarapin through a Huntington town-record reference to planting. The source does not establish the exact swamp location.
translation_content:
No separate linguistic translation is given. Quarapin appears as a personal name preserved in a swamp and planting-place record.

Why Place Names Matter

“Such stories are endless, scattered everywhere on the map of North America. Place names are rich historical documents.”

— William Cronon, Names on the Land: Place Names as Historical Evidence (2018), Section III, concluding paragraph
preservation_content: Quarapin preserves the name of a person and planting place in Huntington, showing how smaller wetlands and fields carried individual and community memory in town records.
